results.name: Cherry-picked window
results.claim: A genuine, FDC-confirmed proof that no payment arrived — over a five-ledger slice chosen to exclude the payment that actually settled this invoice.
results.whyItFools: A naive integration verifies the Merkle proof and marks the invoice. Every field it would check is authentic.
results.defence: markDelinquent requires the proof's request body to reproduce the invoice's own search range, amount, payee and destination tag.

results.name: Fabricated debt
results.claim: A truthful proof that an invoice naming an innocent account went unpaid — for a debt that account never agreed to.
results.whyItFools: The proof is impeccable. Nothing in an attestation can say whether the obligation was ever real.
results.defence: A delinquency reaches a payment record only if the named debtor admitted the debt first, by making any payment carrying the invoice's destination tag from their own XRPL account.
results.reason: invoice marked delinquent; payer record still 0 delinquent / 0 settled

results.name: Cross-chain substitution
results.claim: A nonexistence proof about XRP mainnet, aimed at an invoice that lives on testXRP. Trivially true there, and every request-body field would match.
results.whyItFools: Verifying a Merkle proof establishes that an attestation is genuine, not that it is about the ledger your obligation lives on.
results.defence: The registry pins its sourceId at deployment and checks it, alongside the attestation type — so the guarantee does not depend on how the verifier happens to be configured.
results.reason: Coston2's verifier declines to produce this proof at all: Attestation type and source id combination not supported: (0x5852505061796d656e744e6f6e6578697374656e6365000000000000000
results.note: Hardening rather than a live exploit on Coston2 today: its FDC attests only (XRPPaymentNonexistence, testXRP). Covered by ProofOrigin.test.js.
